kalpataru_hero_headline: What if you could manifest your deepest desires naturally?
kalpataru_hero_sub: The world's easiest and fastest healing and manifestation technique — bestowed upon humanity, completely free, by Moksha Guru Sri Jeeveswara Yogi.
kalpataru_intro_para:
What if the life you are living today is only a fraction of what is truly possible? What if deep healing need not take years, and manifestation need not be a struggle — but could unfold naturally, through pure inner harmony?

Kalpataru is the sacred bridge between the reality you are living and the extraordinary life you were always meant to live. Named after the celestial wish-fulfilling tree, this rare and profound practice was once a closely guarded secret within the highest spiritual traditions. Out of pure compassion, Moksha Guru Sri Jeeveswara Yogi has revealed it to the world as a divine blessing — offered through Siva Kundalini Sadhana entirely free of cost. Kalpataru is not merely a technique; it is a direct, living experience that begins, at once, to transform every dimension of your existence.
kalpataru_intro_highlight: Kalpataru is not something you believe in — it is something you experience.
kalpataru_principle_para: At the heart of the universe lies one absolute truth: everything is Energy (Shakti), and everything is Consciousness (Shiva). Kalpataru aligns them both.
kalpataru_pillar_1: Everything is Shakti (Energy) and Shiva (Consciousness) — and Kalpataru brings the two into perfect harmony.
kalpataru_pillar_2: It heals at the causal level, working across the Sthula, Sukshma, and Karana bodies — so the root itself dissolves.
kalpataru_pillar_3: Not belief, not imagination — transformation you witness for yourself, in your own life.
kalpataru_works_title: Shift Your Frequency, Transform Your Reality
kalpataru_works_para:
Conventional methods ask you to struggle endlessly against your outer circumstances. Kalpataru takes a beautifully different path — it elevates the consciousness of the one who is experiencing life.

Think of the health, abundance, and peace you long for as a high-frequency station, and your present struggles as a low-frequency one. Through Kalpataru and Gurudev's divine energy, your inner frequency is gently tuned away from the low vibration of lack and suffering, and raised to the frequency of healing and fulfilment. As your thought waves sync with this higher state, outer limitations dissolve of their own accord. You need not fight your circumstances at all — when your inner world shifts, your outer reality shifts with it.
kalpataru_step_1: Recognise what you wish to heal or manifest.
kalpataru_step_2: Connect with the divine energy through the sacred technique.
kalpataru_step_3: Healing occurs at the causal body — the root of all karma.
kalpataru_step_4: As your consciousness shifts, your desire manifests effortlessly.
kalpataru_works_highlight: The outer world is simply a reflection of the inner. Change the frequency within, and reality reshapes itself.
kalpataru_levels_para: Most methods treat only the surface symptom, and so the same suffering returns. Kalpataru works far deeper — across all three layers of your being.
kalpataru_level_1: Healing of physical ailments and manifestation in the material world. Practitioners often witness something extraordinary: pain moving through the body from one place to another, before dissolving entirely into nothingness — revealing that the origin of pain is rarely where it appears.
kalpataru_level_2: Transformation of the mind, emotions, and energy patterns, restoring you to profound inner peace.
kalpataru_level_3: Dissolution of karmic imprints at the deepest level — the very root of all recurring struggle.
kalpataru_levels_closing: By clearing these karmic imprints at the causal level, Kalpataru breaks the cycle of suffering itself. Whether it is health, relationships, finances, success, or inner peace, the transformation is complete and lasting — and the same challenges do not come back.
kalpataru_manifest_title: Become the Conscious Creator of Your Destiny
kalpataru_manifest_para:
Kalpataru does more than heal — it awakens the power of manifestation that already lives within you. You do not merely manifest a single desire; you awaken your whole potential to become the conscious creator of your own life.

The journey begins with small, immediate manifestations. Then, step by step, that ability multiplies — until the right opportunities, the right people, deep emotional freedom, and absolute clarity begin flowing into your life of their own accord. You stop merely reacting to life, and begin consciously creating it.
kalpataru_manifest_highlight: When your consciousness, your energy, and your desire align in one frequency — manifestation becomes effortless.
kalpataru_brings_1: Heal physical and emotional pain at its very root.
kalpataru_brings_2: Clear thinking, steady focus, and confident decisions.
kalpataru_brings_3: Relationships restored through love, trust, and understanding.
kalpataru_brings_4: Freedom from fear, trauma, and repeating emotional patterns.
kalpataru_brings_5: Prosperity, success, and fulfilment flowing in naturally.
kalpataru_brings_6: An ever-deepening connection with your true Self.
kalpataru_proof_para: Across the world, thousands of practitioners have already stepped onto this sacred path — and for them, Kalpataru is no longer a technique they practise, but a way of living. From the healing of chronic, life-altering conditions to the fulfilment of lifelong dreams, the miraculous has quietly become their everyday reality.
kalpataru_proof_highlight: For thousands across the world, Kalpataru is no longer a practice they follow — it has become the way they live.
kalpataru_cta_para:
Are you ready to heal at the absolute root?
Are you ready to rise above your karma?
Are you ready to manifest your highest potential — effortlessly?

Begin your journey of healing and manifestation through this sacred practice revealed by Moksha Guru Sri Jeeveswara Yogi. The doorway to your highest potential stands open, and Gurudev's gift is waiting for you.
kalpataru_cta_highlight: With a pure heart, this sacred Kalpataru technique can fulfil any desire. The only limit to what you may attain is your own imagination.

vision_text: To create a world where every human being is given the opportunity to realize their highest potential and transform into a divine being — living with wisdom, compassion, and unity with universal consciousness. We aspire to build an environment that nurtures inner growth, uplifts humanity, and fosters harmony across the planet.
mission_text: To guide the transformation of human consciousness (Jeeva) into divine consciousness (Shiva) — helping individuals move beyond limitations of the ego and awaken to higher awareness, inner peace, and oneness with the universal Self.

guru_journey_quote: I am not here to prove that I am God, I am here to prove that you are God
guru_journey_para1:
Moksha Guru Parama Pujya Sri Jeeveswara Yogi was born on 22nd July 1986, under the star of Shravana, in the old quarter of Hyderabad — the first child of Srimati Anasuya Devi and Sri Manikyam, devout devotees of Lord Shiva. Born with an awakened Kundalini, he carried a rare quality of wonder even as a small child. By the age of five, the simplest of things — a passing object, his own hand, the vast open sky — would fill him with awe, and he would gaze upon them so intently that he seemed to merge with them completely.

His spiritual journey truly began at the age of eight, through a miracle that would shape the rest of his life. One day a saint came to his school and taught meditation to all the children, and from then on a few quiet minutes were set aside for it each morning. During one such session, Gurudev slipped effortlessly into a deep state of Samadhi that lasted four hours — awakening only to find his teachers and classmates gathered around him in astonishment. From that day, a burning curiosity was kindled within him: an unquenchable longing to understand the boundless inner stillness he had touched.
guru_journey_para2:
By the age of thirteen, Gurudev's quest to find the Divine had grown into an irresistible calling. One day, with not a rupee in hand and without a word to anyone at home, he resolved that God-realisation alone would be his life's purpose, walked to the central bus stand, and boarded a bus to Srisailam, the sacred abode of Lord Shiva. When the conductor asked for his fare, the boy answered with quiet certainty that he was going to Srisailam where his parents were — and the elderly stranger seated beside him gently paid the fare for them both, though none could have known that this humble companion was none other than Lord Shiva Himself.

Taking the boy to his own dwelling, the Supreme Guru revealed wonder after wonder across three sacred days. Sent for the darshan of Srisailam Mallanna, Gurudev found the temple entirely empty but for himself and, overcome with joy, embraced the Shiva Linga and remained in the highest state of consciousness for over an hour. On another day, his Supreme Guru placed a lifeless insect in his palm and, with turmeric, vermilion, and a few sacred chants, restored it to life before his very eyes.

Recognising his companion as the very Supreme Guru descended to guide him, Gurudev bowed and asked for initiation. The Supreme Guru granted him Mantra Deeksha on one loving condition — that he return home, for a great sorrow would soon visit his family, and they would need him. With Srisailam Mallanna as witness he received this profound initiation, and it was the last time he would behold his Supreme Guru in physical form.
guru_journey_para3:
Back in Hyderabad, life unfolded just as his Supreme Guru had foretold. Three months later, the sudden passing of his father placed the weight of the entire household upon young Gurudev's shoulders — the family's livelihood, his mother's strength, and the education of his younger brother and sister. He rose to every duty without complaint: delivering nearly four hundred milk packets by bicycle before dawn, tending the family shop late into the evening, and caring for his siblings — yet never once letting go of his sadhana, which he took up faithfully each night once the world had gone to rest.

His practice deepened in the most solitary of places — beside a cremation ground near his home, and at the Jeeva Samadhi of the great Yogi Sri Kesava Swami, who had lived some three centuries before. So intense was his sadhana that his body would at times grow still for hours before returning to normal, and many extraordinary powers awakened within him; during one penance, a stranger's photograph even revealed 116 gods and goddesses surrounding him.

Through more than twenty-four years of unbroken practice, he came to behold 618 of his past lives — recalling in each the form he had taken and the sadhana he had followed — and even the very purpose of his birth was revealed to him. In time he attained Enlightenment. Though his heart longed to enter Jeeva Samadhi, his Supreme Guru redirected him towards a far greater calling — to serve humanity — and so, leaving behind a flourishing career, he devoted his whole life to sharing the sacred knowledge of Kundalini Sadhana.
guru_journey_para4:
In keeping with his Supreme Guru's guidance, Gurudev married and embraced the life of a householder. After the birth of his second child, and as his Supreme Guru had directed, he left the career he had served for nine years to answer his true calling. In 2017, he founded Siva Kundalini Sadhana — a non-profit spiritual organisation devoted to offering this rare and powerful practice, freely, to every soul who seeks it.

At the heart of his mission lies a simple, radiant conviction: that liberation is the birthright of every human being. Gurudev shares his teachings without cost, condition, or prerequisite, and his methods have already brought profound transformation to over 100,000 lives. Anchored in the values he holds dear — Surrenderance, Practice, Service, Gratitude, and Acceptance & Forgiveness — he continues to guide seekers across the world towards the discovery of their own inner divinity.
guru_journey_para5:
Moksha Guru Sri Jeeveswara Yogi is among the rarest of masters — one who bestows Shaktipatham, the direct transmission of spiritual energy from Guru to disciple, awakening the seeker's dormant Kundalini and accelerating their journey within. Alongside it, he offers the sacred grace of Shivapatham, gently guiding disciples towards the ultimate realisation of their own true nature.

What was once shared with only a chosen few, Gurudev has extended to the many. On the night of Maha Sivaratri, he transmitted Shaktipatham to 2,316 seekers in a single night — a feat unprecedented in human history, honoured with a place in the Asia Book of Records. Through this divine grace, countless souls continue to be drawn from darkness into the light of self-realisation.
kundalini_science_para1: Kundalini is the primordial cosmic energy that lies coiled — three and a half times — and dormant at the base of the spine. Portrayed as a sleeping serpent, this divine feminine force is the very source of creation: the same power that gives rise to the entire universe, rests silently, within every human being, life after life. In truth, every spiritual path ever known is connected, directly or indirectly, to the awakening of this one sacred energy — for once it is fully awakened, it leads the seeker to Self-realisation and liberation itself.
kundalini_section_tech_title: A Sacred Science and Inner Technology
kundalini_tech_para: Kundalini Yoga is not mere mysticism — it is the most ancient technology known to humanity, a precise inner science through which we realise our fullest potential. Just as we harness modern technology in daily life, this timeless technology is meant to be used, carrying human consciousness to its ultimate completeness. It is also known as Laya Yoga, the path of dissolution: as the awakened energy rises to the crown chakra, the individual self merges — laya — into Shiva, the infinite. This is the very meaning of yoga: the union of the individual soul with the Supreme.
kundalini_highlight_tech: Kundalini is not superstition — it is the most ancient and precise technology known to humanity.
kundalini_science_para2: Within us flow 72,000 subtle channels, or nadis — and among them three are supreme: Ida, Pingala, and Sushumna. When awakened through Gurudev's grace and sincere Sadhana, the Kundalini enters the Sushumna and rises from the Mooladhara at the base of the spine to the Sahasrara at the crown, passing through the seven principal chakras one by one. Each chakra it awakens, unveils a higher state of consciousness and gently dissolves the physical, emotional, and mental blocks held within it. As the energy finally reaches the crown, Shakti unites with Shiva, and the seeker is drawn into Samadhi — the blissful union of the individual with the Divine.
kundalini_section_steps_title: The Path of Awakening, Step by Step
kundalini_steps_intro:
Siva Kundalini Sadhana unfolds this journey as a clear, systematic progression — taught as graded levels and known not through belief, but through each seeker's own direct experience. Gurudev first opens the seeker's Brahmarandra, the subtle aperture at the crown, so that pure cosmic energy may descend from above and gently awaken the dormant Kundalini — making the awakening remarkably safe and effortless. From there, the path unfolds stage by stage:

1. Awakening — the Kundalini, the Sushumna nadi, and the chakras are awakened from their dormant state.
2. Purification — the awakened energy centres are cleansed, making the path of Kundalini energy ahead clear.
3. Control — the seeker gains steady command over these inner energies.
4. Opening of Petals — each chakra is opened completely, petal by petal, to its full radiance.
5. The Point of No Return — as the energy reaches the Ajna (third eye), the Kundalini can no longer slip back into the lower chakras.
6. Completeness — the Kundalini reaches the Sahasrara, and the seeker attains completeness.

Because Gurudev awakens this energy directly through Shaktipatham, his grace works uniquely for each seeker — for one the Kundalini may awaken fully on the very first day, for another over days or weeks — always unfolding exactly as is best for them.
kundalini_highlight_steps: You need not believe blindly — do the practice, and the truth reveals itself in your own experience.
kundalini_science_para3:
Kundalini awakening is neither dangerous nor reserved for a chosen few. By its very nature this divine energy only nurtures us — as a mother would never harm her own child. Difficulties arise not from Kundalini itself, but from unsystematic practice or the absence of a realised Guru. Learned under the guidance of Moksha Guru Sri Jeeveswara Yogi, Siva Kundalini Sadhana is simple, safe, and profoundly effective: the pure cosmic energy it draws upon brings only wellbeing, quietly easing the burdens of body and mind.

Gurudev's aim is never to make seekers dependent upon him, but to awaken within each person the strength to resolve their own life's challenges and to walk their path with freedom. Offered free of cost and open to every walk of life, this Sadhana harmonises one's worldly life even as it awakens the divine within. Preserved in the Vedic tradition for millennia, this timeless science is offered by Gurudev, today, to all who sincerely seek it.

chakra_what_are_body:
Chakras are energy centers through which life energy continuously flows. They receive energy from the universe and radiate energy back into their surroundings, sustaining both the gross physical body and the subtle body.

There are 114 chakras in total. Of these, 112 chakras are located within the human system, while 2 exist outside the physical body. One lies just above the Sahasrara (Crown Chakra), and the other is located below the Muladhara (Root Chakra). These two external chakras are not experienced as physical structures but may be perceived only as subtle energetic sensations.

Among the 112 chakras within the body, 7 are major chakras, 21 are minor chakras, and 84 are micro chakras. When people generally refer to "the chakras," they are usually referring to the seven major chakras.
chakra_activation_body:
Chakra activation and Kundalini awakening are not the same.

Since chakras are energy centers, they are always active. Whether Kundalini is awakened or not, the chakras continuously receive, circulate, and radiate energy as part of the body's natural functioning.

Kundalini awakening is a separate and much deeper process. It is often compared to a key unlocking a series of locks. Each chakra is like a locked lotus. As Kundalini rises through a chakra, that chakra gradually unfolds and expresses its full spiritual potential.

A chakra may be highly active in a worldly sense even without Kundalini awakening. For example, an artist may possess extraordinary creativity, a leader may possess great influence, or a speaker may possess exceptional communication skills because the corresponding chakra is naturally strong.

However, when Kundalini passes through a chakra, its expression is no longer limited to worldly abilities. The same chakra begins to function at a higher spiritual level, transforming the sadhak's consciousness rather than simply enhancing worldly qualities.
chakra_how_kundalini_body:
Different spiritual traditions describe the awakening of Kundalini in different ways.

Some traditions teach a bottom-up approach, in which Kundalini gradually rises from the Muladhara Chakra to the Sahasrara Chakra, awakening each chakra along the way.

Other traditions describe a top-down approach. In this method, the universal energy — identified with Shiva — is first invoked from above. When this descending energy touches the dormant Kundalini resting in the Muladhara Chakra, Kundalini awakens and begins its upward journey toward the Sahasrara.

This process is often symbolically compared to Lord Shiva descending from Mount Kailasa to unite with Goddess Parvati (Kundalini). After their union, both ascend together to Kailasa, symbolizing the return of awakened consciousness to its highest state.

During this journey, Kundalini may temporarily pause at a chakra if energetic blocks are present. In some cases, it may even return to the Muladhara and remain dormant until those blocks are cleared.
chakra_blocks_title: Blocks, Balance, and the Opening of the Chakras
chakra_blocks_body:
The petals of each chakra are traditionally described as being folded like the petals of an unopened flower. As Kundalini awakens and rises through the chakras, these petals gradually unfold.

Every chakra functions best when its energy is balanced. If a chakra becomes overactive, its energy is excessive. If it becomes underactive, its energy is insufficient. Both conditions create imbalance.

This is similar to body temperature. A healthy body functions within a normal temperature range. Temperatures that are too high or too low both indicate imbalance. Likewise, a chakra requires balanced energy to function harmoniously.

Blocks are energetic obstructions that interfere with the natural flow of energy through a chakra. These blocks often develop during childhood through emotional conditioning, fear, confusion, or conflicting experiences. Spiritual practice gradually removes these blocks, allowing the chakras to return to their natural state of balance.
chakra_physical_body:
As Kundalini interacts with the chakras, practitioners may experience various physical sensations.

Some people experience a sensation of cold, while others experience warmth or heat. Both are considered natural experiences during spiritual practice.

Other common sensations include feelings of spinning, pulling, pulsations, heaviness, or subtle energetic movement. A spinning sensation may appear either clockwise or counterclockwise, and both are considered equally natural.

Some practitioners also experience temporary discomfort during meditation. If these sensations arise only during meditation and naturally subside shortly afterward, they are traditionally understood as signs that energetic blocks are being cleared. This should be distinguished from ordinary physical pain caused by illness or injury.
chakra_root_desc:
The Muladhara Chakra is located at the very base of the spine, at the point where the body rests while sitting. When this chakra first comes into one's awareness, it is perceived as a subtle sensation near the tail end of the spine, almost as if a small portion is gently touching or extending downward. This is not a sensation within the gross physical body but one experienced at a subtler level.

Muladhara is associated with the Earth element, which represents stability, grounding, and physical existence. Hunger is explained as a reduction in the body's internal earth element. Since food itself comes from the earth, eating replenishes this element, restoring balance and vitality.

The presiding deity of Muladhara is Lord Ganesha, the remover of obstacles. His association with this chakra symbolizes the importance of establishing a strong and stable foundation before progressing further on one's journey.

This chakra governs survival, physical health, and the instinct to sustain life. It influences our basic needs — such as food, shelter, safety, and the ability to continue living from one day to the next. A person whose life revolves primarily around meeting daily necessities is said to be functioning predominantly from the Muladhara Chakra.

Individuals with a strongly active Muladhara are often described as natural builders — hardworking, persistent, and resilient, with a strong determination to overcome challenges through consistent effort. Their defining qualities are endurance, discipline, and the ability to build a stable life through dedication and perseverance.

In its natural state, the Muladhara Chakra is said to open fully by approximately seven years of age. However, emotional blocks often begin forming during early childhood through conflicting messages, fear, and insecurity. Because Muladhara serves as the foundation of the chakra system, its proper development is essential — if this chakra does not open fully, the higher chakras cannot awaken in their natural sequence.
chakra_sacral_desc:
The Svadhishthana Chakra is located around the waist, approximately at the level where a belt is worn. It is associated with the Water element, which symbolizes flow, adaptability, creativity, and relationships.

Thirst is understood as a reduction in the body's internal water element. Drinking water replenishes this element from an external source, restoring its natural balance. Just as water is essential for sustaining physical life, the Water element within the body is considered essential for maintaining harmony and vitality.

The presiding deity of Svadhishthana is Lord Brahma, the Creator. Reflecting Brahma's creative nature, this chakra governs creativity, relationships, and the ability to form meaningful connections with others.

Svadhishthana becomes especially active during puberty, when a person naturally begins seeking deeper relationships and emotional connections. The natural desire to connect, create, and build relationships is considered an expression of this chakra.

People with a strongly active Svadhishthana Chakra are often described as natural creators. Creativity becomes one of their defining qualities, allowing them to express themselves through imagination, innovation, and artistic ability. Artists, musicians, writers, and designers are commonly cited as examples of the worldly expression of this chakra.

In its natural state, the Svadhishthana Chakra is said to open fully by approximately fourteen years of age, allowing creativity, emotional expression, and healthy relationships to develop naturally.
chakra_solar_plexus_desc:
Manipuraka is the third and final chakra associated with the material world. Located at the navel, Manipuraka is governed by the Fire element, closely associated with the body's internal temperature. A normal body temperature of approximately 98.4°F is described as the ideal balance of this element. Just as a fever or unusually low body temperature indicates physical imbalance, a chakra with either excessive or insufficient energy is also considered to be out of balance.

The presiding deity is Lord Vishnu, the sustainer, together with Goddess Lakshmi. Accordingly, Manipuraka governs willpower, financial prosperity, worldly success, influence, and personal power.

This chakra corresponds to the stage of life in which a person pursues education, career, financial security, social recognition, and worldly achievements. Individuals with a strongly active Manipuraka are naturally drawn toward positions of leadership, authority, and influence. Politicians are often cited as a classic example of this chakra's worldly expression.

An important characteristic of Manipuraka is that a person may achieve extraordinary worldly success purely through the strength of this chakra, even without Kundalini having awakened through it. However, that success remains directly dependent on the chakra's energetic strength — as long as it remains strong, success continues; as its energy declines, that success may gradually diminish as well.

During spiritual practice, as energetic blocks within this chakra begin to clear, some practitioners may experience physical reactions such as nausea. These are signs that blocks are clearing. If no energetic blocks are present, Manipuraka is said to open naturally by around 21 years of age.
chakra_heart_desc:
Anahata is the bridge between the material and spiritual worlds. Located at the heart center, this chakra is associated with the Air element, symbolized by the continuous flow of the breath — inhalation and exhalation.

Among all seven chakras, Anahata occupies a unique position. The three chakras below it — Muladhara, Svadhishthana, and Manipuraka — govern material life, while the three chakras above it — Vishuddhi, Ajna, and Sahasrara — govern spiritual evolution. Anahata serves as the connecting bridge between these two dimensions.

Its presiding deity is Lord Shiva in His Saguna (manifest) form, traditionally depicted with matted locks, the Tripundra markings, and the serpent Vasuki around His neck.

Anahata governs love, compassion, and caregiving. It naturally becomes prominent during the stage of life associated with marriage, family, and raising children, where feelings of love, responsibility, and nurturing arise spontaneously.

Individuals with a strongly active Anahata are naturally caring, compassionate, and service-oriented. Doctors, nurses, counselors, and others in caregiving professions are often cited as examples of people for whom this chakra plays an essential role. Without a reasonably active Anahata, sustained success in professions centered on caring for others may be difficult.
chakra_throat_desc:
Vishuddhi is the first chakra associated with the spiritual world. Located at the throat, Vishuddhi corresponds to the Space (Ether / Akasha) element, representing the space required for movement and flow.

The first five chakras — from Muladhara through Vishuddhi — are collectively known as the five-element body (Pancha Bhuta Sharira), as each chakra corresponds to one of the five gross elements.

The presiding deity of Vishuddhi is the Jiva (Individual Soul). Upon reaching this chakra, the seeker begins to realize: "I am not this gross physical body, which is composed of the five elements." This marks the beginning of genuine spiritual awareness and the shift from identification with the physical body toward the realization of one's true nature.

Vishuddhi governs communication, self-expression, and the ability to articulate thoughts with clarity. Individuals with a strongly active Vishuddhi are naturally gifted speakers, teachers, and communicators.

As the blocks within Vishuddhi are gradually cleared, the seeker's awareness of Space (Akasha) begins to expand. The seeker may naturally develop a deeper interest in higher subtle dimensions, astral travel, and extraordinary spiritual experiences. However, these experiences are not the ultimate goal — they are simply indications that awareness is becoming subtler. The true transformation is the direct realization: "I am not this gross physical body." As this realization deepens, the seeker's identification with the physical body gradually dissolves.
chakra_third_eye_desc:
Ajna is the second chakra associated with the spiritual world. Situated between the eyebrows, Ajna possesses a unique structural symbolism. Although commonly described as having two petals, each of the two primary petals contains 48 sub-petals — totalling 96. This number is significant: the total petals of the first five chakras (4+6+10+12+16 = 48) is represented in each primary petal.

Ajna is not associated with any of the five gross elements. Instead, it corresponds to the mind. Its presiding deity is Ishwara, Shiva in His Nirguna (formless) aspect — beyond the five afflictions, beyond karma, and beyond latent impressions from previous births.

At the Ajna Chakra, the goal is not to suppress, control, or eliminate thoughts. Instead, one learns to remain as a witness. Thoughts continue to arise, but they are observed without attachment, judgment, or identification. Transformation is the process of dissolving every thought, emotion, perception, limiting belief, conditioned pattern, attachment, fear, and false identity into peace by remaining as the witness, until all that remains is pure awareness.

When the blocks within Ajna are cleared, the sadhak directly realizes that he is not the mind, but the awareness that witnesses it. Ajna governs intuition, deep contemplation, discernment, and foresight.

Once the realization "I am not the body; I am not the mind" becomes firmly established, the seeker no longer falls back into previous states of identification. For this reason, Ajna is often regarded as the "Point of No Return" on the spiritual path.
chakra_crown_desc:
Sahasrara is the third and final chakra associated with the spiritual world. Located at the crown of the head, Sahasrara is associated not with the body or the mind, but with the Atman — the true Self.

Sahasrara is traditionally described as the thousand-petalled lotus. Gurudev presents a more detailed symbolic calculation: the petals of the first five chakras total 48; combined with Ajna's 96, the total becomes 144; multiplied by 1,000 results in 1,44,000 petals — the symbolic petal count attributed to Sahasrara.

At the Sahasrara Chakra, the spiritual journey reaches its culmination. The silent and purified mind naturally dissolves into pure Consciousness. The individual soul (Jiva) realizes its complete oneness with Universal Consciousness (Ishwara). The limited personal identity dissolves into the universal identity. The illusion of separation disappears, and duality (Dvaita) gives way to the direct realization of non-duality (Advaita).

The seeker realizes: "I am not this body. I am not this mind. I am the formless, limitless, infinite Consciousness (Shiva). There is nothing apart from Me. Everything that exists is Me. I am Siva. Sivoham."

Sahasrara is intimately associated with Nirvikalpa Samadhi, the highest state of spiritual absorption. Once the awakened Kundalini reaches the Sahasrara, Nirvikalpa Samadhi is said to arise naturally, without deliberate effort. At this stage, there is only pure awareness, infinite peace, and the direct experience of oneness. Those whose lives are completely dedicated to spiritual realization — such as accomplished yogis — are described as functioning primarily from the Sahasrara Chakra. If no energetic blocks are present, a person is said to be capable of naturally reaching Sahasrara by approximately 49 years of age.

onb_slide1_body:
A non-profit spiritual organisation founded by Parama Pujya Sri Jeeveswara Yogi Gurudev — dedicated to guiding every soul on the path to Moksha.

Salvation is the birthright of every human being. Freely given, open to all, with no barriers or prerequisites.
onb_slide1_quote: Liberation is not reserved for the few. It is the birthright of every human being.
onb_slide2_body:
Born with an awakened Kundalini, Gurudev entered Samadhi at age 8. At 13, he set out alone to Srisailam — where Lord Shiva himself appeared as his Guru and bestowed Mantra Deeksha.

After 24+ years of unbroken Sadhana and attaining Enlightenment, he left a flourishing career to devote his entire life to humanity.
onb_slide2_quote: I am not here to prove that I am God. I am here to prove that you are God.
onb_slide3_body:
Kundalini is the primordial cosmic energy lying coiled at the base of the spine — the very source of creation, resting within every human being.

When awakened through Sadhana, it rises through the seven chakras, dissolving all blocks, unveiling higher consciousness, and leading the seeker to Samadhi — union with the Divine.
onb_slide3_quote: Kundalini is not a metaphor. It is a living force within you, waiting to be awakened.
onb_slide4_body:
Progress through four graded levels of Kundalini Sadhana — from Brahmarandhra Opening to full Kundalini Activation. Each level unlocks as you complete the previous, ensuring deep integration.

Watch video lessons at your own pace. Residential courses with Gurudev are available after online completion.
onb_slide5_body:
Build a steady daily spiritual practice with the built-in Meditation Timer. Choose free meditation or set a specific duration — every session is saved so you can witness your own growth.

Set gentle morning and evening reminders and let Sadhana become as natural as breathing.
onb_slide6_body:
Immerse yourself in devotional Bhajans, Sivoham chanting, and sacred mantras. The music of the divine carries its own shakti — it purifies the atmosphere and stills the mind.

Set the Sivoham mantra as your ringtone and fill every moment with vibration. Dress your home screen with Gurudev wallpapers.
onb_slide7_body:
You are not alone on this path. A global family of seekers walks alongside you, held in Gurudev's boundless grace.

Every step you take in Sadhana — however small — brings you closer to the light that has always lived within you.

🙏 Jai Gurudev 🙏
onb_slide7_quote:
I am not here to prove that I am God. I am here to prove that you are God.
— Sri Jeeveswara Yogi Gurudev
